title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Medical Waste

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Environmental Pollution by Solid Wastes, with a view to strengthening the safe management of medical waste, preventing the spread of diseases, protecting the environment, and safeguarding human health.

Article 2 For the purpose of these Regulations, medical waste means the waste with direct or indirect infectiousness, toxicity or other hazards generated by medical and health institutions in medical treatment, prevention, health care and other related activities.
The classification catalogue of medical waste shall be formulated and published jointly by the competent administrative department of health under the State Council and the competent administrative department of environmental protection under the State Council.

Article 3 These Regulations apply to the activities of collection, transportation, storage, disposal and supervision and management of medical waste.
Domestic waste generated by patients with infectious diseases or suspected infectious diseases admitted by medical and health institutions shall be managed and disposed of as medical waste.
The management of waste narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, radioactive drugs, toxic drugs and related wastes discarded by medical and health institutions shall be subject to the relevant laws, administrative regulations and relevant national provisions and standards.

Article 4 The State promotes centralized and harmless disposal of medical waste and encourages research and development of technologies for safe disposal of medical waste.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for organizing the construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities.
The State shall provide appropriate support for the construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities in remote and poverty-stricken areas.

Article 5 The competent administrative department of health of the people's governments at or above the county level shall carry out unified supervision and management of the prevention and control of diseases in the activities of collection, transportation, storage and disposal of medical waste; the competent administrative department of environmental protection shall carry out unified supervision and management of the prevention and control of environmental pollution in the activities of collection, transportation, storage and disposal of medical waste.
Other relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and management related to medical waste disposal within their respective duties.

Article 6 Any entity or individual shall have the right to report, complain about, inform against and accuse illegal acts committed by medical and health institutions, centralized medical waste disposal units, and supervision and management departments and their staff.

Article 7 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall establish and improve the responsibility system for medical waste management, with their legal representatives as the first responsible persons, who shall earnestly perform their duties to prevent the spread of infectious diseases and environmental pollution accidents caused by medical waste.

Article 8 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall formulate rules and regulations related to the safe disposal of medical waste and emergency plans in case of accidents; set up monitoring departments or full-time (or part-time) personnel responsible for inspecting, supervising and implementing the management of medical waste within their respective units to prevent violations of these Regulations.

Article 9 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall provide training on relevant laws and professional technologies, safety protection, emergency response and other knowledge to the personnel engaged in the collection, transportation, storage, disposal and management of medical waste within their respective units.

Article 10 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall take effective occupational health protection measures, equip personnel engaged in the collection, transportation, storage, disposal and management of medical waste with necessary protective supplies, conduct regular health examinations; and when necessary, provide immunization for relevant personnel to prevent harm to their health.

Article 11 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Environmental Pollution by Solid Waste, implement the hazardous waste transfer manifest management system.

Article 12 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall register medical waste, and the registration contents shall include items such as the source, type, weight or quantity, handover time, disposal method, final destination, and signature of the handler. The registration records shall be kept for at least three years.

Article 13 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall take effective measures to prevent the loss, leakage, or spread of medical waste.
When loss, leakage, or spread of medical waste occurs, medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall take emergency measures to reduce harm, provide medical treatment and on-site rescue to infected persons; and at the same time, report to the health administrative department and the environmental protection administrative department of the local people's government at the county level, and notify units and residents that may be harmed.

Article 14 No unit or individual shall transfer, purchase, or sell medical waste.
It is prohibited to discard medical waste during transportation; it is prohibited to dump or pile up medical waste at non-storage sites, or mix medical waste with other waste and household garbage.

Article 15 It is prohibited to mail medical waste.
It is prohibited to transport medical waste by railway or air.
Where there is a land route available, it is prohibited to transport medical waste by water; where there is no land route and it is necessary to transport medical waste by water, the transportation by water shall be subject to the approval of the environmental protection administrative department of the people's government at or above the city with districts, and may be carried out only after strict environmental protection measures have been taken.
It is prohibited to carry medical waste together with passengers on the same means of transport.
It is prohibited to transport medical waste on water bodies within drinking water source protection areas.

Article 16 Medical and health institutions shall promptly collect the medical waste generated by their units, and place it in special leak-proof and puncture-proof packaging or closed containers according to categories.
Special packaging and containers for medical waste shall have clear warning signs and warning instructions.
The standards for special packaging and containers for medical waste and the regulations on warning signs shall be jointly formulated by the health administrative department and the environmental protection administrative department of the State Council.

Article 17 Medical and health institutions shall establish temporary storage facilities and equipment for medical waste, and shall not store medical waste in the open air; the temporary storage period for medical waste shall not exceed two days.
Temporary storage facilities and equipment for medical waste shall be located away from medical areas, food processing areas, personnel activity areas, and household garbage storage sites, and shall be equipped with obvious warning signs and safety measures such as leak-proof, rodent-proof, mosquito and fly-proof, cockroach-proof, anti-theft, and prevention of children's contact.
Temporary storage facilities and equipment for medical waste shall be regularly disinfected and cleaned.

Article 18 Medical and health institutions shall use special leak-proof and spill-proof transport tools, and collect and transport medical waste to the temporary storage site in accordance with the internal medical waste transport time and route determined by the unit.
After use, the transport tools shall be promptly disinfected and cleaned at a designated location within the medical and health institution.

Article 19 Medical and health institutions shall, in accordance with the principle of nearby centralized disposal, promptly hand over medical waste to centralized medical waste disposal units for disposal.
High-risk wastes such as culture media, specimens, and preservation solutions for bacteria and viruses containing pathogens in medical waste shall be disinfected on site before being handed over to centralized medical waste disposal units for disposal.

Article 20 Sewage generated by medical and health institutions and excreta of infectious disease patients or suspected infectious disease patients shall be strictly disinfected in accordance with national regulations; they may be discharged into the sewage treatment system only after reaching the discharge standards prescribed by the state.

Article 22 Entities engaged in centralized medical waste disposal activities shall apply to the competent environmental protection administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level for a business license; entities that have not obtained a business license shall not engage in activities related to centralized medical waste disposal.

Article 24 The storage and disposal facilities of a centralized medical waste disposal unit shall be located far from residential areas (villages), water source protection zones, and main traffic arteries, with an appropriate safety protection distance from factories, enterprises, and other workplaces, and shall comply with the provisions of the competent environmental protection administrative department of the State Council.

Article 25 A centralized medical waste disposal unit shall collect and transport medical waste from medical and health institutions at least once every two days, and shall be responsible for the storage and disposal of medical waste.

Article 26 A centralized medical waste disposal unit that transports medical waste shall comply with the state provisions on the management of dangerous goods transport and shall use special vehicles with obvious medical waste markings. The special vehicles for medical waste shall meet the requirements for leak-proof, spillage-proof, and other environmental protection and hygiene requirements.
After use, the special vehicles for transporting medical waste shall be promptly disinfected and cleaned at the centralized medical waste disposal site.
The special vehicles for transporting medical waste shall not be used to transport other articles.
Article 27 A centralized medical waste disposal unit shall ensure safety during the transportation of medical waste and shall not discard or spill medical waste.
Article 28 A centralized medical waste disposal unit shall install online monitoring devices for pollutant discharge and shall ensure that the monitoring devices are regularly in normal operation.
Article 29 A centralized medical waste disposal unit shall, when disposing of medical waste, comply with the environmental protection and hygiene standards and specifications prescribed by the state.

Article 30 A centralized medical waste disposal unit shall, in accordance with the provisions of the competent environmental protection administrative department and the competent health administrative department, regularly test and evaluate the environmental pollution prevention and hygiene effects of the medical waste disposal facilities. The test and evaluation results shall be kept in the files of the centralized medical waste disposal unit, and shall be reported to the local competent environmental protection administrative department and the competent health administrative department once every six months.

Article 31 A medical waste centralized disposal unit that disposes of medical waste shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, charge medical waste disposal fees to medical and health institutions.
The medical waste disposal fees paid by medical and health institutions in accordance with the provisions may be included in medical costs.

Article 32 All regions shall utilize and renovate existing solid waste disposal facilities and other facilities for centralized disposal of medical waste, and shall meet basic environmental protection and sanitation requirements.

Article 33 For cities that have no centralized disposal facilities or have insufficient disposal capacity, within one year from the date of coming into force of these Regulations, cities at or above the level of a city divided into districts shall complete the construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities; county-level cities shall complete such construction within two years. The construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities in counties (banners) shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government.
During the period before the centralized medical waste disposal facilities are completed, the relevant local people's governments shall organize the formulation of transitional medical waste disposal plans that meet environmental protection and sanitation requirements, and determine the methods of medical waste collection, transportation, and disposal, as well as the disposal units.

Article 34 The competent administrative departments of health and the competent administrative departments of environmental protection of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and according to their respective duties, conduct supervision and inspection over medical and health institutions and medical waste centralized disposal units.

Article 35 The competent administrative departments of health of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall conduct regular supervision and inspection or irregular spot checks on the disease prevention and control work in the collection, transportation, storage, and disposal of medical waste by medical and health institutions and medical waste centralized disposal units, as well as on the health protection of staff.

Article 36 The competent administrative departments of environmental protection of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall conduct regular supervision and inspection or irregular spot checks on the environmental pollution prevention and control work in the collection, transportation, storage, and disposal of medical waste by medical and health institutions and medical waste centralized disposal units.

Article 37 The competent administrative departments of health and the competent administrative departments of environmental protection shall regularly exchange the results of supervision and inspection and spot checks. Where potential hazards are discovered in medical and health institutions or medical waste centralized disposal units during supervision and inspection or spot checks, they shall order the immediate elimination of such hazards.

Article 38 After receiving reports, complaints, accusations, and charges against medical and health institutions, medical waste centralized disposal units, and supervisory and administrative departments and their staff for violating the provisions of these Regulations, the competent administrative departments of health and the competent administrative departments of environmental protection shall promptly verify the facts, handle the matter according to law, and publish the results of the handling.

Article 40 Where infectious disease transmission or environmental pollution accidents occur due to improper management of medical waste, or where there is evidence proving that infectious disease transmission or environmental pollution accidents are likely to occur, the competent administrative departments of health and the competent administrative departments of environmental protection shall take temporary control measures, evacuate personnel, control the scene, and, as necessary, order the suspension of operations that cause or may cause infectious disease transmission or environmental pollution accidents.

Article 41 Medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units shall cooperate with the relevant departments in inspection, monitoring, investigation, and evidence collection, and shall not refuse or obstruct, nor provide false materials.

Article 42 If a local people's government at or above the county level fails to organize the construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities or to organize the formulation of transitional medical waste disposal plans in accordance with these Regulations, the people's government at the next higher level shall circulate a notice of criticism, order it to complete the construction of centralized medical waste disposal facilities or to formulate transitional medical waste disposal plans within a specified time limit; and may impose administrative sanctions on the principal leaders of the government and the responsible persons in charge according to law.

Article 43 If the competent administrative department of health, the competent administrative department of environmental protection, or any other relevant department of a people's government at or above the county level fails to perform its supervision and inspection duties in accordance with these Regulations, fails to timely handle illegal acts found in medical and health institutions and centralized medical waste disposal units, fails to timely take measures to reduce harm when a communicable disease transmission or environmental pollution accident occurs or is likely to occur, or commits any other act of dereliction of duty, neglect of duty, or malfeasance, the people's government at the same level or the relevant department of the people's government at a higher level shall order it to make corrections and circulate a notice of criticism; if the act causes a communicable disease transmission or environmental pollution accident, administrative sanctions of demotion, removal from office, or expulsion shall be imposed on the principal responsible persons, responsible persons in charge, and other directly responsible persons according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 44 If the competent administrative department of environmental protection of a people's government at or above the county level, in violation of these Regulations, issues a business license to a centralized medical waste disposal unit, the people's government at the same level or the competent administrative department of environmental protection of the people's government at a higher level shall circulate a notice of criticism, order it to revoke the illegally issued license; and may impose administrative sanctions on the principal responsible persons, responsible persons in charge, and other directly responsible persons according to law.

Article 48 If a medical and health institution, in violation of these Regulations, discharges sewage or excrement of patients with communicable diseases or suspected patients with communicable diseases that do not meet the national standards into the urban drainage network, the competent administrative department of construction of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a specified time limit, give a warning, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan; if it fails to make corrections within the specified time limit, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the act causes a communicable disease transmission or environmental pollution accident, the original licensing department shall temporarily withhold or revoke the practice license; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 49 If a medical and health institution or a centralized medical waste disposal unit, when medical waste is lost, leaked, or spread, fails to take emergency handling measures or fails to timely report to the competent administrative department of health and the competent administrative department of environmental protection, the competent administrative department of health or the competent administrative department of environmental protection of the local people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, order it to make corrections, give a warning, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan; if the act causes a communicable disease transmission or environmental pollution accident, the original licensing department shall temporarily withhold or revoke the practice license or business license; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 50 If a medical and health institution or a centralized medical waste disposal unit, without justifiable reasons, obstructs law enforcement personnel of the competent administrative department of health or the competent administrative department of environmental protection in performing their duties, refuses law enforcement personnel to enter the site, or fails to cooperate with the inspection, monitoring, investigation, and evidence collection of the law enforcement department, the competent administrative department of health or the competent administrative department of environmental protection of the local people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, order it to make corrections and give a warning; if it refuses to make corrections, the original licensing department shall temporarily withhold or revoke the practice license or business license; if the act violates the Public Security Administration Punishments Law of the People's Republic of China and constitutes an act violating public security administration, the public security organ shall impose punishment according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 51 In rural areas where conditions for centralized disposal of medical waste are not available, if a medical and health institution fails to dispose of medical waste in accordance with the requirements of these Regulations, the competent health administration department or the competent environmental protection department of the people's government at the county level shall, within their respective functions, order corrections within a specified time limit and give a warning; if corrections are not made within the time limit, a fine of not less than RMB 1,000 yuan but not more than RMB 5,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the spread of infectious diseases or an environmental pollution accident is caused, the original licensing authority shall suspend or revult the practice license; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 52 If any entity engages in the collection, transportation, storage, disposal or other activities of medical waste without obtaining an operating permit, the competent environmental protection department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the immediate cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the illegal gains, and may also impose a fine of not more than one time the illegal gains.

Article 53 Where medical waste is transferred, traded, mailed, or transported by railway or air, or transported by water in violation of these Regulations, the competent environmental protection department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the transferor, transferee, mailer, or consignor to immediately cease the illegal act, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are RMB 5,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the illegal gains shall be concurrently imposed; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than RMB 5,000 yuan, a fine of not less than RMB 5,000 yuan but not more than RMB 20,000 yuan shall be concurrently imposed.
If a carrier knowingly transports medical waste in violation of the provisions of these Regulations despite the consignor's violation, or if the carrier carries medical waste together with passengers on the same vehicle, the carrier shall be punished in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 54 If a medical and health institution or a centralized medical waste disposal unit violates the provisions of these Regulations, causing the spread of infectious diseases or an environmental pollution accident, and thereby causing damage to others, it shall bear civil liability for compensation according to law.

Article 55 The management of wastes with direct or indirect infectivity, toxicity or other hazards arising from family planning technical services, medical scientific research, teaching, autopsy and other related activities shall be carried out in accordance with these Regulations.

Article 56 The management of medical waste from military medical and health institutions shall be subject to the measures formulated by the health competent authority of the Chinese People's Liberation Army by reference to these Regulations.
Article 57 These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
